resources.string: Precise location
Lets the app read the device\'s exact coordinates when Android allows location access.
Precise coordinates show where a person lives, works and regularly spends time.
Approximate location
Lets the app read the device\'s approximate location — usually accurate to a neighbourhood.
Even an approximate location reveals the city and district a person is in.
Location in the background
Lets the app request location even when you are not using it.
Background access makes a continuous movement history possible without any action from you. Android asks for this permission separately.
Photo location tags
Lets the app read the coordinates stored inside photo files.
Photo metadata often records where a picture was taken.
Camera
Lets the app take photos and record video when Android allows camera access.
The camera is one of the most sensitive sensors on the device. Android shows an indicator while it is in use.
Microphone
Lets the app record audio when Android allows microphone access.
Apps with microphone access may capture audio near the device while the system allows microphone use. Android shows an indicator while it is in use.
Read contacts
Lets the app read entries from your address book.
An address book holds data about other people as well as about you.
Modify contacts
Lets the app add and change entries in your address book.
Changes to contacts can go unnoticed.
List of accounts
Lets the app see the accounts added to the device.
The list of accounts reveals which services you use.
Read calendar
Lets the app read the events in your calendar.
Calendar events show a person\'s routine, their meetings and who attends them.
Modify calendar
Lets the app create and change calendar events.
Events can be added without any action from you.
Read SMS
Lets the app read the SMS messages on the device.
SMS carries confirmation codes and private correspondence.
Send SMS
Lets the app send SMS messages.
Messages can be sent without your knowledge, and may cost money.
Receive SMS
Lets the app receive incoming SMS messages.
The app sees incoming messages, including confirmation codes.
Receive MMS
Lets the app receive incoming MMS messages.
MMS can contain private photos and text.
WAP service messages
Lets the app receive WAP push service messages.
These messages are handled without being shown to the user.
Cell broadcast messages
Lets the app read broadcast messages from the mobile network.
Normally used by system emergency-alert apps.
Phone state
Lets the app read the state of the mobile connection and details of the SIM card.
Phone state reveals the carrier and information about calls.
Phone number
Lets the app read the device\'s phone numbers.
A phone number is a stable identifier that makes a person easy to recognise.
Place calls
Lets the app start a phone call without opening the Phone app.
Calls can be placed without confirmation, and may cost money.
Answer calls
Lets the app answer incoming calls.
Used by calling apps and headsets.
Voicemail
Lets the app add messages to voicemail.
Normally used by carrier apps.
SIP calls
Lets the app make internet calls over SIP.
Used by IP telephony apps.
Call handover
Lets the app continue a call that started in another app.
Used by calling apps.
Manage its own calls
Lets the app manage the calls it creates itself.
An ordinary permission for communication apps.
Read call log
Lets the app read the history of incoming and outgoing calls.
A call log shows who a person talks to, and how often.
Modify call log
Lets the app add and delete entries in the call history.
Call records can be changed without it being obvious.
Process outgoing calls
Lets the app see outgoing calls and redirect them.
The permission is deprecated, but it still exposes the numbers being dialled.
Read files
Lets the app read files in the device\'s shared storage.
Shared storage holds documents, downloads and photos.
Write files
Lets the app change files in shared storage.
On recent versions of Android this permission has a much narrower effect.
Photos
Lets the app read images from the shared gallery.
Photos often capture private moments, and carry location tags.
Videos
Lets the app read video files from shared storage.
Video recordings can contain private material.
Audio files
Lets the app read audio files from shared storage.
Access is limited to music and audio recordings.
Selected photos and videos
Gives the app access only to the files you picked yourself.
This is limited access: the app sees only the files you selected.
Manage media files
Lets the app change and delete media files without asking each time.
Files can be modified without a prompt.
Body sensors
Lets the app read body sensors, such as heart rate.
Health readings are among the most sensitive kinds of personal data.
Body sensors in the background
Lets the app read body sensors while you are not using it.
Health readings can be collected continuously without any action from you.
Physical activity
Lets the app tell whether you are walking, running or travelling by vehicle.
Activity data says something about a person\'s daily routine and movement.
Scan for Bluetooth devices
Lets the app look for Bluetooth devices nearby.
The set of devices nearby is an indirect clue to a place and its surroundings.
Connect over Bluetooth
Lets the app connect to paired Bluetooth devices.
The app can see which devices you use.
Bluetooth visibility
Lets the app advertise itself to other Bluetooth devices.
Used for transferring data between devices nearby.
Nearby Wi-Fi devices
Lets the app detect Wi-Fi devices nearby.
Nearby Wi-Fi can be used to work out a location.
Ultra-wideband
Lets the app measure the distance to UWB devices.
Used for precise positioning at close range.
Post notifications
Lets the app show notifications.
An ordinary permission that most apps use.
Do Not Disturb
Lets the app change Do Not Disturb settings.
The app can turn silent mode on and off.
Display over other apps
Lets the app draw windows on top of other apps.
Windows drawn over other apps can cover what is underneath them. Android does not tell third-party apps whether this access is switched on.
Install apps
Lets the app offer to install other apps.
Installing apps from outside a store is one of the most far-reaching capabilities there is. Android does not tell third-party apps whether the user granted it.
Usage statistics
Lets the app read usage statistics for other apps.
Usage history shows what a person uses and when. Android does not tell third-party apps whether this access is switched on.
All files access
Lets the app work with every file in shared storage.
This is the broadest file access there is. Android does not tell third-party apps whether it is switched on.
Modify system settings
Lets the app change some system settings.
Device settings can change without any action from you. Android does not tell third-party apps whether this access is switched on.
Exact alarms
Lets the app schedule tasks to run at an exact time.
Exact timing lets an app wake up in the background on a regular schedule.
Exact alarms (for alarm clocks and calendars)
The app declares itself an alarm clock or calendar and can schedule exact timings.
It is granted without a prompt, which is why Google limits what may use it.
Accessibility service
The app contains an accessibility service.
An accessibility service that is switched on can read the contents of the screen and act on the user\'s behalf.
Notification access
The app contains a notification listener service.
A notification listener sees the contents of every notification, messages included.
VPN service
The app contains a VPN service.
A VPN carries all of the device\'s network traffic through itself.
Device admin
The app contains a device administration component.
An active device admin can set lock policy and erase data.
Unrestricted battery use
Lets the app ask to be excluded from battery optimisation.
Without battery limits an app keeps running in the background for longer.
List of all apps
Lets the app see every installed app.
The set of apps a person has installed says a good deal about them on its own.
Camera in a foreground service
Lets the app use the camera in a foreground service with a notification.
A foreground service extends camera access beyond active use of the app.
Microphone in a foreground service
Lets the app use the microphone in a foreground service with a notification.
A foreground service extends microphone access beyond active use of the app.
Location in a foreground service
Lets the app read location in a foreground service with a notification.
A foreground service extends location access beyond active use of the app.
Health data in a foreground service
Lets the app work with health sensors in a foreground service.
A foreground service extends access to health readings.
Start at boot
Lets the app start after the device restarts.
A common permission for apps that do background work.
Internet access
Lets the app send and receive data over the network.
Almost every app has this permission.
Photos and videos
Lets the app read images and videos.
Limited access to the gallery.
